title: Components of Creative Arts and Sports
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Creative Arts and Sports; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts and Sports teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Draw the bass and treble staves together on the board; notes are named in words on the phone.

skills.key_step: The child names the elements of verse: line, stanza, rhyme, rhythm, refrain and imagery.
representations: a short poem on the board
contexts: a verse for a school festival

board.do: Point at the repeated last line.

misconceptions.ask: What is a stanza?
misconceptions.repair: Count the groups of lines in a poem: each is a stanza.

misconceptions.ask: What is rhyme?
misconceptions.repair: Underline the last words of two lines: cat and hat rhyme.

misconceptions.ask: What is a line of verse?
misconceptions.repair: Point at one row of words: that is a line.

listen_for: words that end with the same sound
misconceptions.ask: What is rhythm in a poem?
misconceptions.repair: Clap a line of a poem; then underline its rhymes.

checks.question: What is rhyme?
checks.answer: the same ending sound in words

checks.question: What is a refrain?
checks.answer: a line or lines repeated in a poem

skills.key_step: The child tells endurance (keeping going without tiring) from agility (changing direction quickly) and names activities for each.

floor.question: Name one skill-related component.
floor.answer: any of: agility, balance, coordination, power, speed, reaction time

steps: Ask: long and steady, or quick changes?

board.do: A shuttle run between cones builds...?

misconceptions.ask: Which is changing direction quickly?
misconceptions.repair: Zigzag between cones (agility), then jog for five minutes (endurance).

misconceptions.ask: Which is lasting a long time without tiring?
misconceptions.repair: Ask "how long can you keep going?" for endurance.

misconceptions.ask: Which activity builds endurance?
misconceptions.repair: Endurance needs a long, steady effort: compare one jump with a 10-minute jog.

misconceptions.ask: Which shows agility: a straight 100 m sprint or a zigzag run?
misconceptions.repair: Time a straight run and a zigzag run.

checks.question: Which builds endurance: long steady running or one jump?

skills.key_step: The child names bass staff pitches (lines G B D F A, spaces A C E G), says the bass clef is for low sounds and writes note values on it.
steps: Lines: Good Boys Do Fine Always.

board.do: Point at the bottom line of the bass staff.

misconceptions.ask: What are the lines of the bass staff from the bottom?
misconceptions.repair: Bass lines: Good Boys Do Fine Always (G B D F A).

misconceptions.ask: What are the spaces of the bass staff from the bottom?
misconceptions.repair: Bass spaces: All Cows Eat Grass (A C E G).

misconceptions.ask: The bass clef is used for...
misconceptions.repair: Sing a low note: that is the bass range.

misconceptions.ask: Where is middle C for the bass staff?
misconceptions.repair: Draw both staves: middle C sits on a ledger line between them.

checks.question: What are the bass staff lines from the bottom?
Is the bass clef for high or low sounds?

skills.key_step: The child groups notes in three-four time: three crotchet beats per bar; a dotted minim fills a bar; a minim and a crotchet make three.

floor.question: How many crotchet beats in a 2/4 bar?

board.do: A minim needs what to fill the bar?

misconceptions.ask: How many crotchet beats are in a bar of 3/4?
misconceptions.repair: Read the top number: 3 beats. Count STRONG weak weak.

misconceptions.ask: How many beats is a dotted minim?
misconceptions.repair: A minim is 2, half of 2 is 1, so the dotted minim is 3.

misconceptions.ask: Which fills a bar of 3/4?
misconceptions.repair: Count the minim: 2. One more beat is needed.

misconceptions.ask: Is a bar of four crotchets correct in three-four time?
misconceptions.repair: Count each bar aloud: 1 2 3, line.

checks.question: How many beats is a dotted minim?
How many crotchet beats in a 3/4 bar?

skills.key_step: The child builds G major: G A B C D E F-sharp G, one sharp (F sharp) on every F, home note G.

floor.question: On which note does C major end?

steps: Write the next seven notes in order.

board.do: Write G A B C D E F G.

misconceptions.ask: G major has one...
misconceptions.repair: Write G A B C D E F G and play it: F needs to be raised, a sharp.

misconceptions.ask: Which note is sharp in G major?
misconceptions.repair: Count the steps: the seventh note, F, must be raised.

misconceptions.ask: On which note does G major begin and end?
misconceptions.repair: The key name is the home note: G major starts and ends on G.

misconceptions.ask: In G major, is every F played as F sharp?
misconceptions.repair: Circle every F in a short G major tune.

checks.question: Which note is sharp in G major?
On which note does G major start and end?
